final_message:
I've stopped before designing anything, so **DESIGN.md hasn't been written yet**. There are still product questions only the product owner can answer. I wrote them to `QUESTIONS.md`, as your instructions say to.

The language and platform were already decided in `substrate.md` (Python 3.11+, standard library only), so the questions are only about what a caller would get back:

1. **How slots line up.** "Aligned to the top of the interval" can mean two things:
   - **(A)** slots start at the beginning of each free gap and repeat every duration;
   - **(B)** slots sit on a fixed grid starting at the opening of working hours.

   With bookings at 09:00–09:45 and 11:00–12:00 and 30-minute slots, the gap between them gives 09:45 and 10:15 under (A), but 10:00 and 10:30 under (B).
2. **Back-to-back bookings.** Can a new booking start exactly when an existing one ends, and end exactly at closing time?
3. **Bad or odd input.** What happens when a booking falls outside working hours, bookings overlap each other, an end time is at or before its start, or the duration is zero?
4. **Time zones.** Are times simple clock times on one day, with no time zones, daylight-saving changes, breaks or gaps between bookings?

Each question has a proposed default, so "accept all defaults" is enough of an answer.

One conflict to know about: `substrate.md` says to write assumptions into the design and carry on. I followed the aims-guide skill and your instructions instead, since Q1 in particular changes which slots come back. The loop is parked in `.aims/state.md` as waiting for answers. When the task restarts with them, it will pick the first design objective, run the required review-and-revise round, and write `DESIGN.md`.
